title: A Path Through the Waypoints: Corners, Smooth Curves, and the Loop That Uneven Spacing Makes

questions.question: A robot follows straight lines between four waypoints on a square route. How sharp is the turn at a corner, in one step?
options: 90.0 degrees: the whole angle in a single step, which no machine can follow
questions.explanation: A curve through the same waypoints turned at most 10.9 degrees in a step.

questions.question: What does the alpha of a Catmull-Rom curve set?
options: How the curve is timed along the way: 0 gives every waypoint the same time, 0.5 the square root of the distance, 1 the distance
questions.explanation: The curve passes through every waypoint whatever alpha is.

questions.question: Waypoints spaced 10, 1 and 14.1. What is the sharpest turn in one step with alpha 0 and with alpha 0.5?
options: 178.2 and 9.1 degrees: uniform timing makes the curve turn back on itself

questions.question: Why does uniform timing loop on uneven waypoints?
options: Every segment gets the same time, so the short step has to be crossed as slowly as the long runs and the curve rushes through it and turns back

questions.question: What happens at a waypoint that is repeated?
options: A distance of zero gives a time interval of zero and a division by it, so repeated waypoints are taken once and the curve function goes straight on a zero interval
It is skipped silently with a warning
questions.explanation: Waypoints on a line with the last repeated stayed exactly on it.

questions.question: What does the curve not do?
options: Say anything about speed, avoid obstacles between waypoints, or help when the waypoints are noisy and the robot only needs to pass near them
questions.explanation: A velocity profile is lesson 14-06's job.
